title: Non-blocking finding from frontend-daily-homework-history-followups-followups-followups-followups's PR review (#414)
description: pr-reviewer's full review of PR #414 (frontend-daily-homework-history-followups-followups-followups-followups) accepted it -- backend/frontend coverage, static analysis (ruff/mypy/eslint/tsc), the profit-target wording guard, validate_tasks.py, and make e2e (28/28) all passed, and the new eslint `no-restricted-imports` override plus the Testing.md tsconfig correction were both independently re-verified as correct. Three non-blocking findings surfaced across the review (one from pr-reviewer's own manual pass, two more from the code-review skill's backgrounded result that arrived after the initial verdict and was folded in as an addendum) and shouldn't disappear once PR #414 merges.

checklist.step: The new `no-restricted-imports` override in frontend/eslint.config.js (scoped to tests/e2e/**/*.ts) is a directory allowlist -- it flags a value import from src/components/, src/features/, src/pages/, src/api/, src/theme/, or an app entry point, and leaves everything else under src/ (type imports anywhere, and both type and value imports from src/utils/) unrestricted. That means a value import from any src/ subdirectory NOT on that six-item list would pass silently -- most notably a future src/hooks/ or src/contexts/ (neither exists in the tree today, confirmed by `find src -maxdepth 1 -type d`), which is exactly the kind of hook/context import the underlying Testing.md convention prohibits, not a borderline judgment call like the src/utils/-purity gap the new doc paragraph does mention. Verified empirically during review: a constructed src/hooks/useFoo.ts (a real `useState`-based hook) imported as a value into a temporary e2e spec produced zero eslint errors. Worth either (a) widening the rule's blocked-group to a broader pattern that catches any new top-level src/ directory by default (with utils/ as the explicit carve-out, revisiting why the earlier gitignore-negation attempt failed for a per-pattern rather than a single-pattern approach), or (b) at minimum, adding a sentence to Testing.md's new paragraph disclosing this second, more clear-cut limitation (a new src/ directory bypasses the check until the allowlist is updated) alongside the src/utils/-purity one it already documents.

The new no-restricted-imports override only inspects static ImportDeclaration/export nodes (confirmed by reading frontend/node_modules/eslint/lib/rules/no-restricted-imports.js -- it registers no ImportExpression visitor), so a dynamic `await import('../../src/features/.../Foo')` in an e2e spec bypasses the rule entirely -- verified empirically: a temporary spec using a dynamic import of a component from src/features/homework/ produced zero eslint errors, while the equivalent static import is correctly flagged. This is a complete bypass of every blocked directory when written as a dynamic import, an inherent limitation of ESLint core's no-restricted-imports rule rather than something fixable within the current approach. No e2e spec in the current tree uses a dynamic import, so nothing is missed today, but worth deciding whether a supplementary check (e.g. a grep-based CI guard, or accepting this as reviewer-only territory and saying so in Testing.md) is warranted, or whether this is acceptable residual risk given how conspicuous a dynamic import in an e2e spec would already look to a reviewer.

The Testing.md paragraph's prose list of blocked directories ("src/components/, src/features/, src/pages/, src/api/, src/theme/, or an app entry point") omits `src/index.css`, even though the actual eslint rule's `group` array in frontend/eslint.config.js blocks it too. Minor completeness fix: add `src/index.css` to the prose list so the paragraph accurately describes the rule's real enforcement.

pr-reviewer's reversed-to-needs_work review of PR #416 found that both rules this task's own fix introduced (the `no-restricted-imports` regex and the `no-restricted-syntax` esquery selector) can be bypassed with a `src/utils/..` path-traversal segment, since a regex over the raw import-source string can't normalize `..` -- `'../../src/utils/../api/homework'` resolves to the blocked `src/api/homework` but neither rule's raw-string match ever sees that. Fix by replacing both built-in-rule-based checks with a single local custom ESLint rule (`e2e-import-guard/no-restricted-src-import`, defined inline in frontend/eslint.config.js) that normalizes the import source with `path.posix.normalize()` before testing it against the blocked-path regex, for both static imports/exports and dynamic `import()` expressions.

Also fix, in the same round (per explicit instruction, rather than leaving them to the already-filed frontend-daily-homework-history-followups-followups-followups-followups-followups-followups follow-up task), the two non-blocking findings from the same review: (1) the `(?!utils/)` negative lookahead incorrectly flagged a bare `src/utils` barrel import (no trailing slash) as blocked; fixed by widening the lookahead to `(?!utils(?:/|$))`. (2) the blocked-path regex was hand-duplicated across two different rule option syntaxes/escapings; fixed by defining it exactly once (`BLOCKED_SRC_VALUE_IMPORT`) and having the single custom rule (which also fixes the path-traversal bypass above) use it for both the static and dynamic cases, eliminating the duplication entirely rather than just synchronizing it.

decisions.decision: Closed gap 1 (directory allowlist) by replacing the eslint `no-restricted-imports` override's `group`-glob pattern with a `regex`-based pattern: `{ regex: '(^|/)src/(?!utils/)', allowTypeImports: true }`. This blocks a value import whose source path contains a `src/` path segment NOT immediately followed by `utils/`, i.e. a true default-deny over all of `src/` with `src/utils/` as the one carve-out, rather than a six-item directory allowlist. Closed gap 2 (dynamic-import bypass) by adding a second rule, `no-restricted-syntax`, with selector `ImportExpression > Literal[value=/(^|\/)src\/(?!utils\/)/]` scoped to the same `tests/e2e/**/*.ts` files -- this visits `ImportExpression` nodes (dynamic `import()`), which `no-restricted-imports` doesn't, and matches the same blocked-path shape against the import's literal source string.
decisions.rationale: For gap 1: the task's background correctly ruled out the `group: ['**/src/**', '!**/src/utils/**']` glob-negation form (the `ignore` package's gitignore-style negation can't re-include a path already excluded by a broader pattern). I confirmed via `frontend/node_modules/eslint/lib/rules/no-restricted-imports.js` that a pattern entry can alternatively supply `regex` instead of `group` -- in that form the match is `group.regexMatcher.test(importSource)`, a plain JS `RegExp#test` against the raw import-source string, with no gitignore semantics at all, so a negative-lookahead regex (`(^|/)src/(?!utils/)`) expresses the exact default-deny-with-one-carve-out semantics that defeated the glob-negation approach. I rejected eslint-plugin-import's `no-restricted-paths` (not currently a frontend dependency; adding a new eslint plugin just for this one rule, when ESLint core's own `no-restricted-imports` already supports a `regex` form I hadn't previously tried, is an unnecessary dependency-weight/maintenance cost) and a custom local rule (unnecessary once the built-in `regex` option was confirmed to work -- a hand-rolled rule would duplicate logic ESLint core already provides correctly). For gap 2: `no-restricted-syntax` is ESLint core (zero new dependency) and its `selector` option is a standard esquery selector; I verified empirically (via `@typescript-eslint/typescript-estree`'s own AST output) that a dynamic `import(...)` parses to an `ImportExpression` node with a `source` child, and that a type-only module reference (`typeof import('./mod')` in a type position) parses to a distinct `TSImportType` node instead, so `allowTypeImports` has no equivalent need here -- an `ImportExpression` is inherently a runtime value expression and can never be a type-only construct. I rejected a grep-based CI guard (strictly weaker than a lint rule already wired into `yarn lint`/pre-commit tooling, and a second enforcement mechanism for the same thing is needless duplication) and leaving it as reviewer-only territory (now avoidable at effectively zero cost once the right ESLint core feature -- `no-restricted-syntax` on `ImportExpression` -- was identified).
decisions.verification: Constructed and ran against real probe files (removed afterward, confirmed via `git status` showing no residual files): (1) a real `useState`-based hook at a non-existent `src/hooks/useProbe.ts`, value-imported into a temp e2e spec -- flagged by `no-restricted-imports`, where it previously passed silently. (2) a dynamic `await import('../../src/features/homework/components/DailyHomeworkHistoryTable')` -- flagged by the new `no-restricted-syntax` rule, where it previously passed silently. (3) a new `src/contexts/MyContext.ts`, value-imported -- flagged. (4) `import '../../src/index.css'` -- flagged (confirming checklist item 3's literal ask, 'add src/index.css to the prose list', is superseded: the rewritten Testing.md paragraph no longer enumerates specific directories at all -- a default-deny regex has no directory list to be incomplete -- so there's nothing left to add src/index.css to; the rule still blocks it, and the doc now says so by construction rather than by naming it). (5) type-only imports from `src/api/homework.ts` and a blocked component's prop type, and a dynamic `import('../../src/utils/format')` -- all correctly pass with zero errors. (6) the two legitimate imports already in `tests/e2e/daily-homework.spec.ts` (the `DailyHomeworkOut` type import and the `formatDate` value import from `src/utils/format.ts`) -- zero errors, unchanged. `yarn eslint tests/e2e` across the whole real suite (no probes) is clean; `yarn lint` repo-wide and `yarn tsc -b --noEmit` both pass with exit 0.
decisions.residual_gap_documented: While verifying gap 2's fix I found and documented (in Testing.md, not left silent) one further residual: a dynamic import whose source is a template literal or variable (e.g. `import(`../../src/${name}`)` or `import(path)`) parses to a `TemplateLiteral`/`Identifier` node rather than a `Literal`, so neither new rule's selector matches it -- verified empirically with a template-literal-sourced probe import, zero eslint errors. I chose not to chase this further: expressing 'the literal source or any string this expression could evaluate to' is a data-flow question no lint-rule selector can answer without executing the code (a custom rule could special-case a few patterns like string concatenation of a literal prefix, but a sufficiently motivated author could always construct a path ESLint's static AST can't resolve), and a dynamically-constructed module path is already a conspicuous, easy-to-flag-in-review pattern for a black-box e2e spec to contain at all -- no spec in the current tree does this. This mirrors the same proportionality judgment the original PR #414 decision made about the gaps it left open.

decisions.decision: Fixed pr-reviewer's reversed-to-needs_work blocking finding (path-traversal bypass of both rules from the prior decision entry) by deleting both the `no-restricted-imports` regex pattern and the `no-restricted-syntax` esquery selector entirely, and replacing them with one local custom ESLint rule, `e2e-import-guard/no-restricted-src-import` (defined inline in frontend/eslint.config.js, registered via a plugin object literal in the `tests/e2e/**/*.ts`-scoped config entry -- no new npm dependency). The rule visits `ImportDeclaration`/`ExportNamedDeclaration`/`ExportAllDeclaration` (static) and `ImportExpression` (dynamic) nodes, and for each checks `path.posix.normalize(rawSource)` against a single shared regex constant (`BLOCKED_SRC_VALUE_IMPORT = /(^|\/)src\/(?!utils(?:\/|$))/`) instead of testing the raw source string. In the same change, fixed both non-blocking findings from the same review round rather than leaving them to the already-filed followup-followup task: widened the negative lookahead from `(?!utils/)` to `(?!utils(?:/|$))` so a bare `src/utils` barrel import (no trailing slash) is correctly exempted instead of false-positively flagged; and eliminated the hand-duplicated pattern by defining the regex exactly once and having the single new rule use it for both the static and dynamic cases (there is no longer a second copy that could drift).
decisions.rationale: Rejected trying to patch the existing regex to also reject a `..` segment without normalizing (e.g. 'block any source containing `/../` beyond its leading prefix') -- that's expressible but fragile: distinguishing the structurally-required leading `../../` (every e2e spec import climbs two directories to reach `src/`) from a later illegitimate `..` requires essentially re-deriving path normalization by hand in regex form, which is exactly what `path.posix.normalize()` already does correctly and is trivially verifiable (confirmed empirically: `path.posix.normalize('../../src/utils/../api/homework')` -> `'../../src/api/homework'`, `path.posix.normalize('../../src/utils/format')` -> unchanged). Rejected keeping the raw-string regex and trying to extend it to detect traversal server-side via a second pattern (double the surface area for the same class of future drift this round is also fixing). A custom rule was the right call once the fix genuinely needed to normalize before testing -- something neither `no-restricted-imports`'s `regex` option nor `no-restricted-syntax`'s esquery selector can do, since both only ever see the raw AST literal/string. Writing one rule that handles both the static and dynamic cases, rather than two rules each normalizing independently, also directly resolves the hand-duplication finding as a side effect rather than requiring a separate shared-constant patch on top of the two-rule structure.
decisions.verification: Constructed probe files covering every shape named in the review and the dispatch instructions (all removed afterward; confirmed via `git status` showing only frontend/eslint.config.js modified, no residual files): (1) static traversal bypass `import { getHomework } from '../../src/utils/../api/homework'` -- now flagged (previously silent). (2) dynamic traversal bypass `await import('../../src/utils/../features/homework/components/DailyHomeworkHistoryTable')` -- now flagged (previously silent). (3) bare `src/utils` barrel import against a real `src/utils/index.ts` probe -- now correctly allowed (previously a false-positive flag). (4) nested `../../src/utils/sub/thing`-shaped import (format.ts) -- allowed, unchanged. (5) ordinary blocked dirs (`src/components/Foo`, a new `src/hooks/useProbe.ts`, a new `src/contexts/ProbeContext.ts`) -- all flagged, unchanged from the prior round's fix. (6) type-only imports from a blocked dir (`import type { DailyHomeworkOut }`) and a blocked component's prop type -- both allowed, unchanged. (7) the known template-literal residual gap (`await import(`../../src/utils/${name}`)`) -- still not flagged, confirmed still a documented residual, not a regression. Ran `yarn eslint tests/e2e/probe.spec.ts` to observe exactly these 5 expected flags and 6 expected non-flags in one pass before deleting the probe. Then ran, against the real tree with no probes: `yarn eslint tests/e2e` (clean), `yarn lint` repo-wide (exit 0), `yarn tsc -b --noEmit` (exit 0), `yarn vitest run` (104 files / 1083 tests passed), `make e2e` (28/28 passed), and `python scripts/validate_tasks.py` (no violations). Updated docs/architecture/Testing.md's "Importing from src/ in an e2e spec" paragraph to describe the new single custom rule, the normalize-then-test mechanism that closes the path-traversal bypass, the bare-barrel exemption, and the single-definition fix for the duplication finding, while preserving (not removing) the honest disclosure of the still-open template-literal/variable dynamic-import residual gap -- the paragraph no longer contains the 'by construction... no such gap' claim pr-reviewer found to be false about path traversal specifically; that claim is now scoped only to the directory-allowlist-vs-default-deny distinction it was originally made about, which remains true.

pr_decision.notes: Independently re-ran everything: backend pytest 1655 passed/99.95% coverage, frontend vitest 1083 passed/104 files at 99.78%/99.06% stmt/branch, backend ruff+mypy clean, frontend eslint+tsc clean, make e2e 28/28, validate_tasks.py clean (396 files) -- all match pr-reviewer's reported figures exactly, not stale. Independently proved the custom rule e2e-import-guard/no-restricted-src-import is genuinely active (flagged a known-bad probe under its exact name, then inverted its internal isBlockedSrcSource boolean and confirmed eslint's output flipped on the same probe) and reproduced both original path-traversal bypass probes (static '../../src/utils/../api/homework' and dynamic import of the same shape) as now flagged, plus the bare-utils-barrel exemption as correctly passing. Separately reproduced pr-reviewer's 'my-package/src/foo' false-positive finding myself against the real rule (confirmed via a probe file, removed after) and weighed it on its own terms: unlike the path-traversal bypass (a silent false negative that defeated the guard's entire purpose and was rightly escalated blocking in the prior round), this is a false positive -- it over-blocks a hypothetical bare-package import that doesn't exist anywhere in the current tree, fails loudly and visibly (a lint error a contributor would see immediately, not a silent hole), and has a cheap, already-identified fix (anchor the regex to a relative-path prefix) tracked on the new followups-followups-followups-followups-followups-followups-followups task. A newly-introduced false positive is not categorically the same risk as a newly-introduced false negative/bypass -- it doesn't undermine the check's purpose, it's self-reporting rather than silent, and nothing in the current codebase trips it -- so deferring it as non-blocking, as pr-reviewer did, holds up under my own standard. Agree the board-bookkeeping convention question (two task ids riding one PR/branch) is a legitimate open question worth deciding but not a merge blocker, since it's explicitly documented via a decisions entry and validate_tasks.py confirms no structural invariant is violated.

comments.summary: ACCEPT, superseding the prior needs_work verdict on this same PR: commit 413f22df deletes both rules that had the raw-string path-traversal bypass (`no-restricted-imports`'s regex option and the `no-restricted-syntax` esquery selector) and replaces them with one local custom rule, `e2e-import-guard/no-restricted-src-import`, that normalizes the import source with `path.posix.normalize()` before testing it against a single shared `BLOCKED_SRC_VALUE_IMPORT` regex. Before trusting this, I first proved the rule is genuinely active rather than silently inert: a known-bad static import (`src/api/homework`) is flagged under the exact rule name `e2e-import-guard/no-restricted-src-import`, and inverting the rule's internal `isBlockedSrcSource` test (negating its return value) flips eslint's output from erroring to clean on the same probe -- the rule's own logic, not a hardcoded pass/fail, drives the result. Then independently reproduced both of my own original traversal-bypass probes (static `'../../src/utils/../api/homework'` and dynamic `await import('../../src/utils/../features/...')`) and confirmed both are now flagged. Stress-tested `path.posix.normalize` edge cases myself: above-root traversal (`'../../../../src/features/x'`) flagged; a bare `src/utils` barrel (no trailing slash) now correctly allowed (previously a false positive, fixed in this same commit by widening the lookahead to `(?!utils(?:/|$))`); `./`-prefixed sources resolve and flag correctly; a trailing-slash directory import flags correctly; the legitimate false-positive set from the prior round (`../../mysrc/foo`, `../../src-gen/foo`) still passes clean. Windows-style backslash sources are not normalized or matched by this rule, but this isn't a real-world bypass -- JS/TS import specifiers are always forward-slash regardless of host OS, so a backslash-written import specifier wouldn't resolve as a valid import at all; not a finding. Confirmed the newly-claimed re-export coverage actually works: `export { Foo } from`, `export * from`, and `export * as ns from` a blocked directory are all flagged (including with a traversal segment), while `export type { X } from` and `export type * from` a blocked directory are correctly left alone. Confirmed type-only handling reproduces the old `allowTypeImports` behavior exactly: `import type { X }`, an all-inline-`type`-specifier import, and a mixed value+type import (correctly flagged, since it carries a real value specifier) all behave as intended. Re-read docs/architecture/Testing.md's full updated paragraph end to end -- every remaining claim (default-deny-vs-allowlist, the normalize-before-test traversal fix, the bare-barrel exemption, the single-definition dedup, and the still-open template-literal/variable dynamic-import residual gap) checks out against the actual rule behavior; the previously-false 'by construction... no such gap' claim about path traversal is gone, and the still-true default-deny claim is preserved. All probe files removed afterward; confirmed via `git status` showing a clean tree.

Non-blocking, new finding (not in prior review rounds): the regex `(^|\/)src\/(?!utils(?:\/|$))` anchors on `(^|/)`, which matches not just a project-relative `src/` segment but also a bare npm package specifier that happens to contain a literal `src/` path segment anywhere in it, e.g. `import { x } from 'my-package/src/foo'` is incorrectly flagged as blocked (verified empirically: `path.posix.normalize('my-package/src/foo')` is unchanged and the regex matches the `/src/` substring right after `my-package`). This is a real false positive, not present in the original six-directory glob-allowlist version of this rule (which only matched specific `**/src/<dir>/**` globs, never a bare `src/` segment in an unrelated package name) -- it was introduced when PR #416 replaced the allowlist with the default-deny regex, and persists unchanged through this round's traversal-bypass fix since the regex's anchor shape didn't change. No e2e spec in the current tree imports a package whose specifier contains a literal `src/` segment, so nothing is misflagged today, but it's the same class of over-restriction as the now-fixed bare-utils-barrel false positive, just on a different input shape. Tracked as a follow-up rather than left only in this comment.

Non-blocking, board-bookkeeping judgment call worth recording: task-worker folded the already-filed follow-up task (frontend-daily-homework-history-followups-followups-followups-followups-followups-followups, tracking two non-blocking findings from this task's own needs_work review) into this same PR #416/branch -- marking its checklist items done, setting its `git.branch` to this task's own branch name rather than a dedicated `task/<its-own-id>` branch, and moving its state in lockstep with this task. This is explicitly decided and documented (a `decisions` entry on that task gives the rationale: avoiding a redundant branch/PR pair for a three-line fix in the same file) and doesn't violate any `validate_tasks.py`-checked structural invariant -- confirmed `python3 scripts/validate_tasks.py` is clean against the current board state. But CLAUDE.md's board conventions don't explicitly document a 'fold a follow-up task into its parent's same-round fix' pattern, and the child task's `git.branch` now diverges from the `task/<task-id>` naming convention CLAUDE.md states, which could trip up any future tooling that derives a task's branch from its id rather than always reading the `git` field. Resolving both tasks' states as part of this accept (see notes) rather than blocking on the pattern itself, since it's a defensible call with a recorded rationale, not an undocumented or silent one -- but worth deciding explicitly whether this pattern should be formalized or avoided going forward.

review.notes: Full re-review of PR #416 after task-worker's fix (commit 413f22df) for the path-traversal bypass this task's own prior needs_work verdict found. Per the dispatch instructions' explicit emphasis, the single most important check performed first: proved the new local custom rule `e2e-import-guard/no-restricted-src-import` is genuinely wired into eslint's flat config and actually drives the lint result, via both a known-bad probe flagged under its exact rule name and a mutation test (inverting its internal boolean test flips eslint's output on the same probe) -- the rule is real, not inert-but-green config theater. Independently reproduced my own original traversal-bypass probes (static and dynamic) and confirmed both are now flagged; confirmed the re-export forms (ExportNamedDeclaration, ExportAllDeclaration, export * as ns) are genuinely covered, including with a traversal segment, since that was newly-claimed coverage nobody had tested yet; confirmed type-only imports (declaration-level, all-inline-specifier, and mixed value+type) behave exactly as the old `allowTypeImports` semantics did; confirmed the bare-`src/utils`-barrel false positive from the prior round is fixed and the hand-duplicated regex/selector pattern is eliminated (not just synchronized) by the single-rule-single-definition design. Re-read docs/architecture/Testing.md's entire updated paragraph against the actual rule behavior -- every remaining claim holds. Ran the full verification suite myself rather than trusting the PR description: backend ruff/mypy clean, backend pytest 1655 passed/99.95% coverage; frontend yarn lint and tsc -b --noEmit clean; frontend vitest run --coverage 99.78%/99.06% statement/branch (no regression from either side's 90% gate); python3 scripts/check_profit_target_wording.py clean; python3 scripts/validate_tasks.py clean (395 files); make e2e 28/28 passed (not strictly required by step 9/9a since this PR touches no application UI code -- only frontend/eslint.config.js, docs, and task-board JSON -- but run anyway per the dispatch instructions and the established precedent from this same task family's earlier rounds, since it's cheap and adjacent to the suite the lint rule governs). No API route/schema touched, so openapi.json regeneration doesn't apply. No new module/dependency/layer added (a local inline eslint rule is dev-tooling, not an application layer), so architecture-review doesn't apply. The code-review skill was dispatched in the background against the diff; its result returned after I'd already drafted this verdict and reported zero findings, consistent with my own manual pass -- confirms rather than changes the accept. Two non-blocking findings surfaced during my own testing beyond what either prior round or the backgrounded code-review caught (a `my-package/src/foo`-shaped false positive from the regex's unanchored `(^|/)src/` match, and the board-bookkeeping pattern of folding the 6-level follow-up task into this PR) -- both detailed above and tracked on a new follow-up task (frontend-daily-homework-history-followups-followups-followups-followups-followups-followups-followups) rather than left only in this PR comment.
